subject.title: fix(config,secrets): emit JSON errors and cover dotenv roots

question: Should `openclaw secrets apply` treat both the resolved state-root `.env` and active config-root `.env` as authorized plaintext-secret migration targets when those roots differ?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically consistent with audit and is covered by focused proof, but expanding deletion to a second user file is a compatibility and secrets-ownership policy choice that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Confirm dual-root cleanup
options.body: Accept the shared helper contract so audit and apply both inspect and scrub the effective state-root and active config-root dotenv files.

options.title: Limit cleanup to one root
options.body: Retain broader audit visibility but constrain apply to a single explicitly owned dotenv location if modifying both roots is not the intended migration policy.

recommendation.title: Confirm dual-root cleanup
recommendation.body: Accept the shared helper contract so audit and apply both inspect and scrub the effective state-root and active config-root dotenv files.
